arm: tt-bio affinity, whole CLI invocation, on one Blackhole p150a
why: The comparison in docs/nesso1.md divided a whole `tt-bio predict --model boltz2` invocation (386.251 s, perf/nesso1/results/tt_boltz2_affinity_512.json) by Nesso-1's forward alone (8.341 s), which credits Nesso-1 with Boltz-2's entire fixed cost. This leg times Nesso-1 the same way the Boltz-2 arm was timed: the real command, wall to wall, fresh --out_dir per rep so featurisation is not served from cache. Same reasoning and same wording as perf/nesso1/results/cli_e2e.json, which is how the H200 arm was timed.
settings: shipped CLI defaults: bf16 trunk, fp32 affinity stacks, 5 recycling steps, 256-token pocket crop

reps.note: First invocation of this shape on this card: the wall is dominated by ttnn kernel compilation, not by the model.
Fresh out_dir, so RDKit conformer embedding and the ESM-2 pass ran again. This is the number a user sees for a single input on a card that has run the model before.

not_matched_on: box load: the Boltz-2 rep ran at loadavg 16-22 on tt-quietbox2, this one on a quieter tt-quietbox
kernel cache state: the Boltz-2 rep records one rep and does not say whether its caches were warm
reps: one on the Boltz-2 side, two here
comparison.read_it_as: An order-of-magnitude reading, and an upper bound on Boltz-2 because a host-heavy pipeline on a box at loadavg 20 runs slower than it has to. The superseded 59x came from dividing this same 386.251 s by the retired 6.50 s pairformer floor, which mismatched the regions and used a number that is no longer the shipped one.
comparison.matched_alternative: gpu_reference.json:boltz2_comparison.matched_marginal, 19.325x cheaper per screened compound at matched protocol on one H200, both arms timed as full CLI invocations with a stated method.
